topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular context of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations can drive cancer when the affected cells and their surroundings permit clonal evolution.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk despite uncertainty about individual outcomes and the influence of inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and host conditions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how biological processing can determine their effects.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why mutational initiation may require subsequent tumour-promoting activity for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and synthesis of carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The developmental-stage examples culminate in a recap that places tissue susceptibility within the preceding account of how carcinogens produce cancer.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how observations from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how controlled experimental tests reveal carcinogenic potential and why their results may not predict human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing distils the lecture's conclusions into a risk–benefit perspective on environmental exposures.
